topic: Meiosis II and Significance of Meiosis
title: Meiosis II: 1 Cell to 4 Cells Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
In the lab book, Aarav saw young pollen grains in little groups of four, each group from just one cell. Meiosis I already halved the chromosomes, so why does the cell divide a second time?

You will see the dyad after meiosis I and interkinesis with no DNA copying, a zoom ladder down to one chromosome, and both cells running meiosis II live: prophase II, metaphase II, anaphase II, telophase II and cytokinesis, ending in a tetrad of four haploid cells. Then why meiosis matters (the same chromosome number every generation, 23 + 23 = 46, and variety from crossing over and random separation), meiosis I vs II side by side, a pause and think, six events sorted, the interkinesis exam trap, an original NEET-pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions. This is Episode 79 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
